scope: Literature-derived research options for ML-TradeEngine. Forecast combination, binary net-utility acceptance, action-value regression, allocation, uncertainty and sequential control are distinct roles. Reviewed methods are not all implemented or tested. Cash, costed equal weight, trend and trailing class priors remain mandatory benchmark controls outside this architecture catalog. LSTM, EnbPI and direct LLM discussion remain in the companion reviews; no direct LLM allocator is proposed for the first selection family. Proposal-aligned primary study: contextual convex expert weighting with a fixed downstream policy. This broader catalogue contains optional later extensions.
priority_note: Baseline/First/Second/Deferred are project-specific research priorities, not numeric performance rankings or deployment approvals. First means a candidate for a bounded registered comparison, not a request to fit every listed boosting package. Only Hedge and logistic forecast stacking are currently planned for the isolated predictive screen; measured results belong in separate result artifacts. Each source supports the general method, while its proposed trading role and priority are research judgments. All learned transforms, feedback updates and labels must respect eligible past data and explicit availability timestamps; every allocator must obey the separate shared risk/execution contract.

models.name: Fixed probability mixture
models.output: A fixed convex combination of expert class probabilities.
models.fit_reason: Isolates whether learned routing adds value over the same experts and information.
models.main_risk: Forecast weights are not asset weights; a fixed mixture can still be miscalibrated.
models.repo_status: A 50:50 linear/tree mixture exists in src/models/adaptive.py; same-expert screen control planned; results separate.
models.source_title: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts — Jacobs et al. (1991), general mixture context

models.name: Regularized logistic forecast stacking
models.output: Three-class probabilities learned from out-of-time expert log probabilities.
models.fit_reason: A compact learned combination tests predictive value with few parameters.
models.main_risk: In-sample expert predictions or random cross-validation leak information; it is not a positive-net-utility classifier.
models.repo_status: Completed exploratory probability screen: two fits and 250 dates in 2025. Not a convex expert gate; no clear advantage over prior. See SCREEN_RESULTS.md.
models.source_title: StackingClassifier — official scikit-learn documentation; temporal folds require a custom design

models.name: Regularized logistic net-utility meta-label
models.output: Probability that a proposed action passes a registered cost-inclusive outcome criterion.
models.fit_reason: Inspectable L2 or elastic-net coefficients provide a small accept/abstain model.
models.main_risk: Positive-outcome probability ignores payoff magnitude; labels must include execution and mature before fitting.
models.repo_status: Design reviewed; distinct from the planned directional stack; no costed meta-label screen established.
models.source_title: Regularization Paths for Generalized Linear Models via Coordinate Descent — Friedman et al. (2010)

models.name: Ridge incremental-utility head
models.output: Estimated net horizon utility difference between each admissible action and a base action.
models.fit_reason: Tests a finite action menu without Bellman bootstrapping; uses current cash, holdings and required turnover.
models.main_risk: Simulated counterfactual labels depend on fill and continuation assumptions; final validation needs a continuous ledger.
models.repo_status: Reviewed proposal; no implemented utility-head evidence established by this catalog.
models.source_title: Ridge — official scikit-learn documentation; incremental-utility target is this project proposal

models.name: Histogram gradient boosting
models.output: Binary acceptance probability; a separate registered regressor could estimate action utility.
models.fit_reason: Existing implementation family supports a small nonlinear challenger with bounded tree capacity.
models.main_risk: Early stopping and threshold choice must use eligible inner data; classification and utility targets are distinct trials.
models.repo_status: Classifier expert exists in src/models/adaptive.py; controller adaptation is not covered by the planned stack/Hedge screen.
models.source_title: HistGradientBoostingClassifier — official scikit-learn documentation

models.name: XGBoost
models.output: Action acceptance probability or a separately registered utility estimate.
models.fit_reason: Existing dependency makes shallow regularized trees a tractable alternative challenger.
models.main_risk: Large search spaces and deep trees can overfit dependent histories; old expert bundles use different contracts.
models.repo_status: Legacy expert family/dependency exists; no comparable new controller result established.
models.source_title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System — Chen and Guestrin (2016)

models.name: LightGBM
models.output: Action acceptance probability or a separately registered utility estimate.
models.fit_reason: Existing dependency offers an alternative efficient tabular implementation.
models.main_risk: Leaf-wise growth needs strict leaf/support limits; published speed results do not predict local trading value.
models.repo_status: Legacy expert family/dependency exists; alternative to the first boosting challenger, not permission to fit all packages.
models.source_title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree — Ke et al. (2017)

models.name: CatBoost
models.output: Acceptance probability, optionally using registered categorical context.
models.fit_reason: Tests whether pooled categorical context adds value if such information is eligible.
models.main_risk: Ordered boosting does not replace chronological purging; target encodings and instrument memorization need controls.
models.repo_status: Absent from inspected requirements.txt; reviewed option; no installation or controller evaluation claimed.
models.source_title: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features — Prokhorenkova et al. (2018)

models.name: Gaussian HMM regime context
models.output: Filtered current-state probabilities supplied to a separately evaluated gate.
models.fit_reason: Tests persistent latent context against observable trend and volatility buckets.
models.main_risk: Full-path smoothing leaks later observations; small state counts, occupancy and refit label remapping need checks.
models.repo_status: src/features/regime.py already forward-filters frozen HMM parameters; a new controller ablation remains separate.
models.source_title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition — Rabiner (1989)

models.name: Linear mixture-of-experts gate
models.output: Nonnegative expert weights summing to one, then a combined class distribution.
models.fit_reason: Extends the existing correctness gate with low-capacity context-dependent routing.
models.main_risk: Correctness is not costed utility; correlated experts and reused calibration/selection data can inflate apparent value.
models.repo_status: Legacy per-expert logistic correctness gate exists in src/models/gating.py; no comparable new net-value result established.
models.source_title: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts — Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton (1991)

models.name: Hedge with delayed feedback
models.output: Expert probability-mixture weights updated only from matured bounded losses.
models.fit_reason: Few parameters isolate whether revealed past performance helps combination.
models.main_risk: Immediate-feedback regret claims do not transfer unchanged; duplicate updates, unresolved labels and portfolio switching costs matter.
models.repo_status: Completed exploratory delayed-feedback screen. Cumulative matured-date loss, no forgetting; no clear advantage over prior. See SCREEN_RESULTS.md.
models.source_title: A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning and an Application to Boosting — Freund and Schapire (1997)

models.name: LinUCB
models.output: Discrete admissible action chosen using predicted reward and an uncertainty bonus.
models.fit_reason: Interpretable exploration baseline if the feedback is genuinely partial.
models.main_risk: Linear reward assumptions and action support may fail; holdings make repeated portfolio decisions stateful.
models.repo_status: Reviewed sandbox option; no new controller implementation or exploration authorization established.
models.source_title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation — Li et al. (2010)

models.name: Linear Thompson sampling
models.output: Randomized admissible action chosen from sampled reward-model parameters.
models.fit_reason: Tests uncertainty-driven exploration against LinUCB under the same feedback model.
models.main_risk: Prior/noise assumptions, delayed rewards and exploration losses require explicit modeling; seed diversity is not new market evidence.
models.repo_status: Reviewed sandbox option; no new controller implementation or evaluation established.
models.source_title: Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoffs — Agrawal and Goyal (2013)

models.name: Constrained single-period optimizer
models.output: Feasible long-only target weights balancing expected return, estimated risk and turnover cost.
models.fit_reason: Directly compares allocation logic while holding forecasts fixed; exposes binding constraints.
models.main_risk: Risk/return horizons and units must agree; solver feasibility and pending cash must map to the actual ledger.
models.repo_status: Reviewed new allocator proposal; existing risk scaling/clipping is not evidence that this optimizer is implemented.
models.source_title: Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization — Boyd et al. (2017)

models.name: Scenario CVaR allocation
models.output: Feasible targets minimizing or constraining estimated scenario tail loss.
models.fit_reason: Tests a tail-risk objective against covariance sizing and fixed caps with identical forecasts.
models.main_risk: Sparse tails, scenario choice and broken cross-asset dependence can create misleading precision; CVaR is not a loss cap.
models.repo_status: Reviewed proposal; no new scenario allocator result established.
models.source_title: Optimization of Conditional Value-at-Risk — Rockafellar and Uryasev (2000)

models.name: Adaptive conformal abstention
models.output: Prediction/utility interval and a registered accept/abstain rule.
models.fit_reason: Separates uncertainty calibration from the underlying forecast and allocation model.
models.main_risk: Marginal interval coverage is not selected-trade coverage or profitability; delayed overlapping outcomes affect validity.
models.repo_status: Reviewed extension; not part of the planned predictive stack/Hedge screen.
models.source_title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift — Gibbs and Candès (2021)

models.name: Small GRU utility head
models.output: Incremental action utility estimated from a short causal sequence.
models.fit_reason: Tests whether temporal patterns add value beyond the same lagged features in a linear model.
models.main_risk: Sequence overlap reduces independent information; scaling, warm-up and hidden-state restart semantics must be causal.
models.repo_status: Reviewed new controller; legacy directional LSTM is a different target/interface and supplies no GRU-controller evidence.
models.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation — Cho et al. (2014)

models.name: Model predictive control
models.output: A planned target sequence; execute only the first action and replan.
models.fit_reason: Tests whether planning future turnover and cash improves on the H=1 optimizer.
models.main_risk: Incorrect horizon forecasts or terminal costs can dominate benefits; requires an H=1 matched ablation.
models.repo_status: Reviewed proposal, deferred behind a qualified single-period allocator; no new MPC result established.
models.source_title: Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization — Boyd et al. (2017)

models.name: Temporal Fusion Transformer
models.output: Multi-horizon forecast or quantiles consumed by a separate controller.
models.fit_reason: Studies richer sequence and covariate forecasting while retaining the same decision contract.
models.main_risk: Known-future covariates must actually be known; data demands, leakage and attention interpretation need controls.
models.repo_status: Reviewed forecaster option; not an allocation controller and not evaluated by the current screen.
models.source_title: Temporal Fusion Transformers for Interpretable Multi-horizon Time Series Forecasting — Lim et al. (2021)

models.name: Chronos pretrained forecasting
models.output: Probabilistic future-value forecasts consumed by a separate controller.
models.fit_reason: Tests a fixed pretrained expert under a frozen checkpoint and preprocessing contract.
models.main_risk: Unknown pretraining overlap and nonstationary financial data limit clean historical zero-shot claims.
models.repo_status: Reviewed forecaster option; no checkpoint acquisition, installation or project performance claimed.
models.source_title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series — Ansari et al. (2024)

models.name: Fitted Q iteration
models.output: Action values fitted to Bellman targets over audited transitions.
models.fit_reason: A simpler batch-RL bridge after supervised utility models and simulator parity.
models.main_risk: Bootstrapped future value and state/action coverage add assumptions beyond one-period utility regression.
models.repo_status: Reviewed sequential-learning proposal; no qualifying transition dataset or new result established.
models.source_title: Tree-Based Batch Mode Reinforcement Learning — Ernst, Geurts and Wehenkel (2005)

models.name: Proximal Policy Optimization
models.output: Distribution over bounded admissible target actions.
models.fit_reason: Potential on-policy baseline after a faithful costed environment exists.
models.main_risk: Reward exploitation, repeated-history overfitting and simulator mismatch can produce misleading returns.
models.repo_status: Reviewed deferred option; no new PPO implementation, training or promotion claimed.
models.source_title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms — Schulman et al. (2017)

models.name: Soft Actor-Critic
models.output: Stochastic continuous action transformed into feasible portfolio targets.
models.fit_reason: Potential off-policy continuous-control comparison after state/transition validation.
models.main_risk: Entropy incentives, replay distribution and feasibility mapping require care; interactions are not independent market histories.
models.repo_status: Reviewed deferred option; no new SAC implementation, training or promotion claimed.
models.source_title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor — Haarnoja et al. (2018)

models.name: Conservative Q-Learning
models.output: Conservatively estimated action values and an extracted feasible policy.
models.fit_reason: Addresses some extrapolation errors in a qualified offline transition dataset.
models.main_risk: Conservatism cannot identify unsupported actions, unobserved market impact or missing portfolio states.
models.repo_status: Reviewed deferred option; action/state support and transition provenance remain prerequisites.
models.source_title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning — Kumar et al. (2020)

models.name: Implicit Q-Learning
models.output: Value/Q estimates with a policy extracted through advantage-weighted behavioral cloning.
models.fit_reason: Alternative offline method that avoids querying out-of-dataset actions during value training.
models.main_risk: Behavior support remains essential; avoiding some extrapolation does not prove safe or profitable portfolio choices.
models.repo_status: Reviewed deferred option; no new IQL implementation, training or supported policy evaluation claimed.
models.source_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Q-Learning — Kostrikov, Nair and Levine (2022)
